what_its_for: Tirbanibulin is a prescription cream used to treat actinic keratosis (rough, scaly patches on the skin caused by years of sun exposure) on the face or scalp. These patches can sometimes turn into skin cancer if not treated, so it is important to use this medicine as directed by your doctor.
how_to_take: Apply a thin layer of this cream to the affected area on your face or scalp once a day for 5 days in a row. Use only enough cream to cover the treatment area (up to about 25 square centimeters, roughly the size of a 2x2 inch square). Wash your hands thoroughly before and after applying the cream. Do not get the cream in your eyes, mouth, lips, or nostrils. If you accidentally get it in these areas, rinse well with water right away. Do not cover the treated area with bandages or wrappings unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Apply once daily for 5 consecutive days. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much area to treat. Do not use more than directed and do not apply it to larger areas than your doctor recommends.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply the cream as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the cream at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze. Dispose of any unused medication properly after your treatment course is complete.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting the cream in your eyes, mouth, nostrils, or on your lips. Avoid touching your face and then touching other people, especially children, without washing your hands first. Avoid applying the cream to areas that are not being treated. Avoid prolonged sun exposure on the treated area. Use sunscreen, wear protective clothing, and limit time in the sun while using this medication and until the treated area heals. Do not use this cream if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant unless specifically directed by your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience any of the following: severe skin irritation, redness, swelling, blistering, or open sores at the treatment site that do not improve or get worse; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; accidental contact with the eyes causing pain, redness, or vision changes; or any other side effects that concern you or do not go away.
when_it_works: Most patients complete treatment after just 5 days of use. The treated skin may look red, flaky, or irritated during and after treatment — this is normal and means the medicine is working. The skin typically heals and the actinic keratosis patches improve within a few weeks after finishing treatment. Your doctor will follow up to check how well the treatment worked.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this cream, as its safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully studied. Women who could become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment. The safety and effectiveness of tirbanibulin in children under 18 years old has not been established. Older adults (65 years and older) may use this medication safely but should follow the same instructions as other adults.
